biography: Born in Hobro, Denmark, Tom Kristensen's journey into motorsport began not on asphalt, but on the icy lakes of Jutland, where he honed his car control drifting on frozen surfaces. His father, a local mechanic, fueled his passion, building his first kart from spare parts. This humble start quickly escalated as Tom dominated the Danish karting scene, attracting the attention of Formula Ford teams. A defining moment came in 1997 when, against all odds and with a shoestring budget, he secured a surprise podium at a wet Hockenheimring in Formula 3, proving his uncanny ability to adapt to challenging conditions. Now at his peak with Audi, Kristensen is a formidable force in endurance racing, known for his meticulous preparation and relentless pursuit of victory.
drivingStyle: Kristensen's driving style is a blend of calculated precision and controlled aggression. He's not one for flamboyant overtakes, preferring to build speed consistently throughout a stint. His mastery lies in his ability to manage tires, extracting maximum performance while preserving their lifespan. In high-pressure situations, he remains remarkably calm, making him a formidable competitor in the closing stages of a race. He often describes his approach as 'driving with the head, not just the foot'.

rivalries.name: Jean-Pierre Dubois
rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track battle during the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2003, culminating in a controversial collision, ignited a long-standing feud.

rivalries.name: Marco Bellini
rivalries.reason: Bellini publicly questioned Kristensen's driving style, labeling it 'too conservative' and sparking a war of words in the motorsport press.

rivalries.name: Kazuki Sato
rivalries.reason: A series of close finishes and near-miss accidents in the American Le Mans Series created a rivalry built on mutual respect, but fierce competition.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky blue socks during races, regardless of weather.
Refuses to eat any food containing tomatoes on race weekends.
Spends 30 minutes visualizing the first lap of the race before getting into the car.
famousQuote: Pressure is a privilege. It means you're in a position to win.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2000 after a grueling battle with the Porsche team, securing his first major international victory and cementing his status as a rising star.
careerLowPoint: Suffering a mechanical failure just an hour from the finish line at the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2005, costing him a certain victory and leaving him visibly devastated.
